source.citation: Baskauf, Steven J. Ulmus americana (Ulmaceae) - leaf - whole upper surface. Photograph, 2 June 2002, Great Smoky Mountains. Bioimages, Vanderbilt University, image 11688. CC BY 4.0.
what_it_does_not_supply: anything about a tree that stood in Chicago in 1812, 1835 or 1904; it is a modern leaf from the Great Smoky Mountains, a botanical analogue for the species' habit (the liberties register L-tree-architecture-2743)
the leaf's colour in the scene: the atlas keeps its near-neutral green and the zone records' July colour stays in charge of the hue
the leaf's outline: the elm blade's shape is still drawn by the tree atlas generator
what_it_supplies: the upper-surface texture of an American elm leaf (Ulmus americana): its straight, close lateral veins and mottle, sampled as lightness into the elm tiles of the leaf atlas model
